name: Kansas
agency: Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks (KDWP)
summary: Kansas is about 97% private land, so most public hunting is on KDWP wildlife areas around the big Corps reservoirs, state fishing lakes, the Cimarron National Grassland, and Walk-In Hunting Access (WIHA): private land KDWP leases so any licensed hunter can hunt on foot. Whitetails here grow big, and nonresident deer permits come through a spring draw.
publicNote: KDWP wildlife areas: many require a free daily check-in (ksoutdoors.com/checkin or the GoOutdoors KS app). Baiting and trail cameras are prohibited on KDWP land and WIHA. WIHA is foot traffic only, no camping, no target shooting; fall tracts are open Sept 1-Jan 31, Nov 1-Jan 31 or Sept 1-Mar 31 (posted on each tract) and spring turkey tracts Apr 1-May 31.

fees.note: Nonresident junior (15 and under) $42.50. Residents 65-74 pay $15.
Nonresident price includes the $27.50 draw application fee. Youth: $12.50 resident, $117.50 nonresident.
Youth spring permit $7.50. 2026 prices; internet fee extra.

rules: Hunter education is required for anyone born on or after July 1, 1957 (verify current exemptions on KDWP).
Deer: blaze orange is required during the youth/disability, muzzleloader and pre-rut antlerless seasons per KDWP's deer page; check the regulations summary for other firearm seasons.
Baiting while hunting or preparing to hunt is illegal on all public lands; trail and game cameras are prohibited on KDWP lands and WIHA.

On KDWP lands: no more than two portable stands/blinds per hunter, marked with your name and address or KDWP number; place no more than 14 days before the season and remove within 14 days after. Portable blinds and decoys can't be left overnight.
Walk-In Hunting Access: open only on posted WIHA signs, on foot only; no camping, target shooting, dog training, horses, fires or trapping (unless the landowner allows trapping).
Many wildlife areas require a free daily check-in before hunting and check-out after.
seasons: Dates not yet published (spring 2026: Apr 1 youth – May 31)
seasonsNote: Big game dates are KDWP's 2026-27 seasons (as reported May 22, 2026). Waterfowl and dove dates follow the federal frameworks; check KDWP's waterfowl page. Fort Riley and Fort Leavenworth have their own deer segments.

areas.name: Walk-In Hunting Access (WIHA)
areas.where: Statewide (private land leased for public hunting)

rut: Whitetail rut peaks in mid-November; the regular firearm season (Dec 2-13) falls after the peak, so archery hunters get the rut.

nr.note: Nonresident deer permits are drawn in April for a single deer management unit. A preference point alone is $27.50.

everywhere: Kansas hunting license (and HIP for migratory birds)
